title: Generic free subtraction with smaller fibre support after a blowup
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme, $n\geq0$, and $f:X\to S$ an affine smooth morphism of relative dimension $n$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] whose fibres are geometrically integral, meaning integral after every residue-field extension. Let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module and $U\subset S$ a quasi-compact open such that $\mathcal F|_{X_U}$ is finitely presented and flat over $U$. There exist a $U$-admissible blowup $b:T\to S$ and a finite affine open covering $T=\bigcup_a T_a$ with the following properties. Put $U_a=T_a\cap b^{-1}(U)$, $X_a=X\times_ST_a$, and $\mathcal F_a=(\mathcal F^b)|_{X_a}$. The family $X_a\to T_a$ is affine smooth of relative dimension $n$ with geometrically integral fibres; $U_a$ is quasi-compact; $\mathcal F_a$ is quasi-coherent of finite type and is finitely presented and flat over $U_a$. There are an integer $r_a\geq0$, a map $\alpha_a:\mathcal O_{X_a}^{\oplus r_a}\to\mathcal F_a$ and an open $W_a\subset X_a$ surjecting onto $T_a$ such that $\alpha_a|_{W_a}$ is an isomorphism. The sequence $0\to\mathcal O_{X_a}^{\oplus r_a}\xrightarrow{\alpha_a}\mathcal F_a\to\mathcal H_a\to0$, with $\mathcal H_a=\operatorname{coker}\alpha_a$, remains exact after pullback along every $T'\to T_a$. The module $\mathcal H_a$ is quasi-coherent of finite type, its restriction over $U_a$ is finitely presented and flat over $U_a$, and for every $t\in T_a$ one has $\dim\operatorname{Supp}((\mathcal H_a)_t)\leq n-1$, with empty support assigned dimension $-1$. Here support is the locus of nonzero stalks and dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; in particular every fibre of $\mathcal H_a$ is zero when $n=0$. Pullbacks are as in [def-pc-module-pullback]. Schemes and quasi-compactness conventions are as in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], quasi-coherence and finite type as in [pqf-def-coherent], finite presentation of module sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], and relative flatness as in [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Admissible blowups retain their finite-type centre ideals [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], and all module strict transforms use those specified ideals [def-trf-module-strict-transform].

source.place: Tag 0815, theorem-flatten-module, proof paragraph 3 through the definition of H and its induction hypotheses; Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre.

proof.text: First apply [lem-pc-smooth-flat]: $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Since $S$ is affine and $X\to S$ is affine, $X$ is affine. The affine finite-presentation criterion [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] makes $f$ finitely presented. The original flatness over $U$ holds in particular at all fibre generic points over $U$. Thus every hypothesis of [lem-trf-generic-free-blowup] holds, and it supplies a $U$-admissible blowup $b:T\to S$ and an open $V\subset X_T$ surjecting onto $T$ on which $\mathcal G=\mathcal F^b$ is finite locally free. Keep its specified centre ideal throughout.

source.place: Tag 0815, theorem-flatten-module, paragraph beginning Next; Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre

proof.text: By [lem-trf-generic-rank-admissible-invariance], applied to the same original family and this one blowup, $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $X_T\to T$ is affine flat of finite presentation with geometrically integral fibres, and $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent of finite type. Over $U_T=b^{-1}U$ it identifies with the original module over $U$, hence is finitely presented and flat there. Also $U_T\cong U$ by [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open], so $U_T$ is quasi-compact. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1), $X_T\to T$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$. No flattening theorem is being invoked here: only the preliminary generic-free blowup of Step 1.

source.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, permanence observations; Tag 0815, theorem-flatten-module, paragraph 3

proof.text: Fix $t\in T$ and take an affine neighbourhood $A\subset T$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Write $X_A=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $N=\Gamma(X_A,\mathcal G)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], $N$ has a finite generating list. Let $\xi$ be the generic point of the integral fibre $(X_A)_t$. The nonempty open $V_t$ contains $\xi$. By [lem-sbc-affine-module-germ-localization], the images of the generators of $N$ span $\mathcal G_\xi\otimes\kappa(\xi)$. Choose a subset forming a basis, of size $r$; send the standard basis to these global sections, using the affine sheaf-module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], defining $\alpha:\mathcal O_{X_A}^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal G|_{X_A}$. Shrink a trivializing open inside $V$ about $\xi$ so its rank is $r$. In these frames $\alpha$ is a square matrix whose determinant is nonzero in $\kappa(\xi)$, hence is a unit in the local ring at $\xi$. The open where that determinant is invertible is an open $W\subset X_A$ containing $\xi$ on which $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. If $r=0$, the trivialization is already the zero module and the same conclusion holds.

source.place: Tag 0815, theorem-flatten-module, paragraph 3: choice of alpha and W; Tag 05I3, lemma-induction-step, existence paragraph

proof.text: The smooth map $X_A\to A$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] makes the image of $W$ an open neighbourhood of $t$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $T_t$ of $t$ inside that image by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Replace $W$ by its inverse image over $T_t$; it now surjects onto $T_t$. Perform this construction for every $t$. Quasi-compactness of $T$ selects finitely many of these affine opens, denoted $T_a$, with their maps $\alpha_a$, ranks $r_a$, and opens $W_a$. Restricting the base-changed family preserves all properties of Step 2; in particular smoothness of relative dimension $n$ follows again from [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1).

source.place: Tag 0815, theorem-flatten-module, paragraph 3: shrink S so W surjects

proof.text: For each $a$, $U_a=T_a\cap U_T$ is quasi-compact. Indeed cover the quasi-compact open $U_T$ by finitely many affine opens of $T$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Their intersections with $T_a$ are quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion](1), since $T$ is quasi-separated, and their finite union is $U_a$. The restrictions of $\mathcal G$ to $X_a$ are quasi-coherent of finite type, and their restrictions over $U_a$ are finitely presented and flat, by Step 2.

source.place: Tag 01KV, lemma-quasi-separated-affine; finite affine subcover argument

proof.text: Fix $a$ and write $T_a=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $X_a=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $N=\Gamma(X_a,\mathcal F_a)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] and [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], $R\to B$ is flat and finitely presented; $N$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]. For every prime of $R$, its fibre is integral and its generic point lies in $W_a$, since $(W_a)_t$ is nonempty open in that integral fibre. There $\alpha_a$ is an isomorphism, and $\mathcal F_a$ is free over $\mathcal O_{X_a}$, hence flat over the base because $X_a\to T_a$ is flat. In the affine stalk identifications of [lem-sbc-affine-module-germ-localization], these are exactly the generic-stalk flatness and residue-field-isomorphism hypotheses of [lem-trf-free-subtraction-flatness]. That node therefore makes $B^{\oplus r_a}\to N$ universally injective over $R$, and gives the equivalence of relative flatness of $N$ and its cokernel at every stalk.

source.place: Tag 0815, theorem-flatten-module, paragraph 3: Tag 05I3, lemma-induction-step, globalized by Algebra Tag 05CL

proof.text: Set $\mathcal H_a=\operatorname{coker}\alpha_a$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] it is quasi-coherent, and its affine module is $Q=N/\operatorname{im}\alpha_a$; the images of finitely many generators of $N$ generate $Q$, so it is of finite type. For an arbitrary $T'\to T_a$, work on each affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R'\subset T'$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] to identify the original quasi-coherent modules with their affine section modules, and [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change] to identify their tensor pullbacks. The pulled-back sequence is associated to $0\to R'\otimes_R B^{\oplus r_a}\to R'\otimes_R N\to R'\otimes_R Q\to0$. Its left map is injective by Step 6, taking the $R$-module $L=R'$; the remaining exactness follows from the quotient presentation of $Q$. Localization preserves this module exactness by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], so it is exact on every stalk and hence as a sheaf sequence on this affine cover and hence on $X_a\times_{T_a}T'$. This proves the asserted universal exactness, including the original sequence by $R'=R$.

source.place: Tag 0815, theorem-flatten-module, paragraph 3: universal injectivity and the definition of H

proof.text: At each point lying over $U_a$, $\mathcal F_a$ is flat over $U_a$ by Step 2. The stalkwise flatness equivalence in [lem-trf-free-subtraction-flatness] therefore proves that $\mathcal H_a|_{X_{U_a}}$ is flat over $U_a$. On that open $\mathcal O^{\oplus r_a}$ is of finite type and $\mathcal F_a$ is of finite presentation. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-presentation-cokernel] makes $\mathcal H_a|_{X_{U_a}}$ finitely presented. Neither conclusion requires global finite presentation of $\mathcal F_a$.

source.place: Tag 0815, theorem-flatten-module, paragraph 3: induction hypotheses for H; Modules Tag 0H96, lemma-cokernel-finite-finite-presentation

proof.text: For $t\in T_a$, the fibre of $\mathcal H_a$ is finite type with closed support $Z_t\subset(X_a)_t$, by [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type]. It vanishes on the nonempty open $(W_a)_t$ because $\alpha_a$ is an isomorphism there. Thus $Z_t$ is a proper closed subset of the integral fibre. By [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $\dim_x((X_a)_t)=n$ for every $x\in(X_a)_t$, with $\dim_x$ as in [def-kun-dimension]. For any chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets $Z_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Z_k$ in $Z_t$, the same subsets are closed in $(X_a)_t$, and appending the irreducible closed set $(X_a)_t$ gives a chain of length $k+1$ in $(X_a)_t$. Pick $x\in Z_0$ and an open $O\ni x$ of $(X_a)_t$. Each member of the chain is irreducible and meets $O$, so its intersection with $O$ is a nonempty open, hence irreducible and dense, subset of it; the intersections form a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $O$, strict because their closures are the original members. Thus $\dim O\ge k+1$ for every such $O$, so $k+1\le\dim_x((X_a)_t)=n$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Hence $\dim Z_t\le n-1$ if $Z_t$ is nonempty. If $n=0$, a nonempty $Z_t$ would already give a chain of length one, a contradiction, so the fibre sheaf is zero. Assigning empty support dimension $-1$, the bound holds for every $t$. If $T$ is empty take the empty finite cover; rank zero and empty $U$ impose no additional conditions. This completes all clauses.
